proposal.hypothesis: A 16×16 output tile with a 16-wide K stage should reuse each staged A and B value across multiple output products compared with the naive one-output kernel. This candidate deliberately uses synchronous shared-memory staging as the control; a later asynchronous candidate can retain its tile, lane, and compute mapping so the copy mechanism is the main difference. No speedup is claimed before measurement.

retained: Replace one-thread-per-output serial dot products with a 16×16 CTA output tile and 16-wide K stages.
Cooperatively stage A and B in shared memory using the same (ty, tx) lane mapping intended for the paired asynchronous candidate; synchronize before consumption and before reuse.
Mask row, column, and K tails with zero-filled loads while preserving full-FP32 accumulation and alpha/beta output semantics.
